reviewer: Codex agent visual inspection; no independent human review
selection: All 3 baseline errors, 2 lowest-margin correct outputs, plus remaining hydrants (7 cases total)

cases.observation: Water covers a lane; no hydrant body is visible.
cases.possible_cause: Caption-dependent ground truth is not identifiable from these pixels. Largest wrong margin among the three errors; cosine margin is not calibrated confidence.

cases.observation: Branches and scattered debris lie across abandoned pavement; waste is spread out rather than a compact household rubbish pile.
cases.possible_cause: Road texture competes with sparse garden-waste evidence; baseline dumping prompts overemphasize piles.

cases.observation: A large discarded appliance rests beside vegetation; no intact streetlight is visible.
cases.possible_cause: Single bulky appliance is under-described by pile-focused prompts; metal housing may resemble fixture debris. Legality requires external context.

cases.observation: Fallen metal lamp/post components lie on paving. Correct but the top-two margin is small.
cases.possible_cause: Broken metal hardware overlaps the visual appearance of signposts and dumped objects.

cases.observation: Bulky furniture and debris sit beside a damaged road. Correct with a small margin.
cases.possible_cause: Pothole-like road texture competes with waste in a wide scene; original center crop may lose peripheral objects.

cases.observation: Water emerges from a pavement opening; no exposed hydrant body. Correct category but source context supports the label.
cases.possible_cause: A correct forced-choice prediction does not demonstrate recognition of an unseen hydrant or the leak source.

cases.observation: A visible hydrant has a tall water plume. Correct and a larger margin than the caption-dependent cases.
cases.possible_cause: This is the clearest visual hydrant example; one clear case cannot establish generalization.
